clue.text: Predict the French will go at the back or front of ship

indicators.note: says the French article is placed after the verb, at the end of the build

parts.note: to predict is to forecast
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to guess whether the French will end up at the stern or the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back or front of ship' reads as one location; 'at the back' belongs to the wordplay and 'front of ship' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the raised forward deck of a vessel, traditionally the crew's quarters near the bow.

clue.text: State of continuous change making one cross after illness

indicators.note: places the cross behind the illness in the build

parts.note: influenza, flu, is a common illness
X is the shape of a single cross

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from sickness is irritable all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective, angry, but it is the letter X, written after FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Flux is a condition of constant movement and instability.

clue.text: Duplicate I placed in special parcel

indicators.note: the single letter is set within the rearranged letters
a special arrangement of the word parcel is an unusual one, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone says they posted a copy of something in a special delivery package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges PARCEL into REPLCA, and 'placed in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, a duplicate of an original.

clue.text: This food may be fatty — so try spinach possibly?

indicators.note: the letters of these three words might possibly be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A diner is told a greasy dish might be swapped for a leafy vegetable instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SO TRY SPINACH. A CORNISH PASTY is a pastry turnover of meat and vegetables from Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty is a pastry-wrapped savoury snack often rich with suet or lard, so it can be greasy.

clue.text: Wash, getting black off wee Tim for inspection

indicators.note: the letter for black comes off the end of the word

parts.note: to scrub is to wash vigorously
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Tiny Tim is the little boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, and wee means tiny

explanation.surface: Little Tim is scrubbed clean of grime before being checked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes B from SCRUB to leave SCRU; 'wee Tim' calls up Dickens's Tiny Tim, giving TINY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, careful examination.

clue.text: Girls in spectacles — not good!

indicators.note: says the letter for good is absent from the word for spectacles

parts.note: spectacles are glasses

explanation.surface: Young women wearing eyeglasses are judged unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from GLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a chiefly Scottish and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Stuff made with cold butter?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a butter is one who butts, as a ram does with its horns

explanation.surface: A question about something prepared with chilled dairy fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' wants to be the dairy spread; read it as 'one that butts', a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff something is to pack it tightly, to force as much in as possible.

clue.text: Down-to-earth common sense is needed in the kingdom

indicators.note: the short word is required inside the word for kingdom

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom

explanation.surface: Practical good judgement is said to be essential throughout the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a practical, unsentimental approach to things as they really are.

clue.text: Award tot (so we hear!) for interfering

indicators.note: says what follows is how the words for award and tot sound when spoken

parts.note: a medal is an award; a tot is a sum, as in to tot up

explanation.surface: A small child is given a prize, apparently for being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler; it is a sum, as in totting up figures. MEDAL SUM said out loud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meddlesome intrudes in other people's affairs.

clue.text: Something crumby seen to be aristocratic?

explanation.surface: Something crumbly turns out to be posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumby' means made of crumbs: the top layer of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The top layer of a loaf is its upper crust; figuratively the phrase means the highest social class, the nobility.

clue.text: Provided cash to get one into accommodation

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes inside the word for lodgings

parts.note: a pad is informal for one's flat or lodgings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone handed over money to get a person into a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid means handed over money owed, settled a bill.

clue.text: Addition of contaminant let loose in a time span

indicators.note: the jumbled short word goes inside the word for a period

parts.note: a duration is a span of time

indicators.note: set loose, the letters of let are freed to move

explanation.surface: A pollutant is released over a period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' reads as release in the surface; 'loose' is the anagram signal on LET, and 'in' places the scrambled letters within the time span.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulteration is the debasing of a substance by mixing in an impure ingredient.

clue.text: Small province at end of motorway

indicators.note: puts the province after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A little region found where a highway finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, written MI; Northern Ireland is often called simply the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini, as in miniskirt or minibus, means small or reduced in size.

clue.text: Exercise machine that could make della trim

indicators.note: the letters of the words could be made into something else

explanation.surface: Della hopes a gym apparatus will slim her down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges DELLA TRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a gym apparatus with a moving belt for walking or running on the spot.

clue.text: Sort of network said to make man or woman angry

indicators.note: says the name is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Chris can be short for Christopher or Christine, so names either sex
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A kind of web is supposedly what makes a person furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the name: Chris is a unisex name, short for Christopher or Christine, which is why the clue says 'man or woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisscross is a pattern of lines intersecting in many directions, like a mesh.

clue.text: Holding out with hesitation, going around suffering pain

indicators.note: turning around means the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
aching is suffering pain

explanation.surface: Someone extends a hand hesitantly, walking around while hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' reverses only the hesitation sound; 'Holding out' means extending, not resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching means stretching out a hand or arm, extending towards something.

clue.text: Economic downturns quietly accepted by poor neighbourhoods

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by the word for deprived areas

parts.note: slums are run-down urban districts
P stands for piano, quietly, in music

explanation.surface: Recessions are suffered without protest in deprived districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump is a sudden severe fall in trade or prices.

clue.text: People who are not thankful could be angriest

indicators.note: the letters of angriest could be another word if reordered

explanation.surface: Ungrateful people might well be the most irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ANGRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person.

clue.text: Boat with a thousand crashing into bridge

indicators.note: the two letters smash their way inside the word for bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch of one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A vessel with a large number aboard smashes into a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in East Asia.

clue.text: Yours truly has a home that's most shabby

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: The speaker owns a house that is the most run-down of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe something poor and squalid, so the superlative is the scruffiest.

clue.text: Ruder man working in a pit?

indicators.note: working implies the letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A coarser miner is at work down the coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges RUDER MAN. 'pit' looks like a coal mine but is the armpit.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit lies beneath the arm, so something in it is located under the upper limb.

clue.text: Normally a contemporary of 24 gets to reign

parts.note: Asa was king of Judah while the clue's answer at 24 ruled Israel, in the Bible
to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A peer of a biblical king gets to be monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Asa was king of Judah in the Bible, in the same era as King Ahab of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually, as is generally the case.

clue.text: Elegant old city facing destruction

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
bane means ruin or cause of destruction

explanation.surface: A graceful ancient city is about to be ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave, polished and courteous in manner.

clue.text: Conservative madman meets the queen — a garrulous type

parts.note: the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland makes hatter a crossword madman, as in mad as a hatter
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A Tory lunatic is introduced to Her Majesty and won't stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer is someone who talks incessantly, a talkative person.

clue.text: King in a garment but it can't be seen!

indicators.note: says the word it is invisible, so removed from the garment

parts.note: a habit is a monk's or nun's robe

explanation.surface: A monarch in clothes nobody can see, like the emperor in the fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it can't be seen' removes IT from HABIT to leave HAB. Ahab was a king of Israel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab was a biblical ruler of Israel, husband of Jezebel.

clue.text: Headland a monstrous location?

explanation.surface: A promontory where a monster is said to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness in Scotland is home of the legendary Loch Ness Monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a promontory, a cape; Ness is also the Scottish loch famous for its monster.

clue.text: There's something wrong in one of these farm animals

indicators.note: the unknown letter sits inside the rearranged word
set wrong, the letters of one are put out of order

parts.note: X stands for an unknown thing, as in algebra

explanation.surface: Something is amiss with one of a herd of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ONE into OEN, and 'in' puts X, an unknown something, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle, especially castrated bulls used as draught beasts on farms.

clue.text: At the eleventh hour — or 59 moments later?

explanation.surface: Just in time, or nearly an hour later.
explanation.walkthrough: An hour has sixty minutes, so after fifty-nine of them the one remaining is the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at the latest possible moment; also, literally, the final sixty-second span of an hour.

clue.text: Place of hatred when power has been taken away

indicators.note: the letter for power is removed from the word for hatred

parts.note: spite is malice or hatred
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A spot of loathing appears once energy has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, a plot or position.

clue.text: Soldiers sitting down to eat cooked greens — people on a mission

parts.note: a mess is where soldiers eat together, and the group dining there

indicators.note: cooked letters of greens are prepared differently, in a new order

explanation.surface: Troops at dinner eat boiled vegetables before setting out on an errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges GREENS into ENGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Messengers are couriers sent to carry word, envoys on an errand.
